description:
## What the code does

`CalendarEventGetParams` carries `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]` at crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/mod.rs:102.

The canonical sibling `EmailGetParams` at crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:40 carries `#[derive(Debug, Default, serde::Serialize)]` — explicitly no `Clone`. Same pattern across the other canonical params structs: `EmailCopyParams` (mod.rs:67), `MailboxSetParams` (mod.rs:87), `EmailSubmissionSetParams` (mod.rs:111), `EmailImportInput` (mod.rs:147), `EmailParseParams` (mod.rs:253). None of them derive `Clone`.

## What idiomatic Rust would do

Considering the signature side: `calendar_event_get` takes `params: Option<CalendarEventGetParams>` by value (consumes the struct). `email_get` takes `params: Option<EmailGetParams>` by value too. In both cases, a caller who wants to reuse the same params for multiple calls (e.g. a paginated fetch loop) needs `Clone` to avoid rebuilding the struct each time:

```rust
let params = CalendarEventGetParams { expand_recurrences: Some(true), ..Default::default() };
for chunk in id_chunks {
    let _ = sc.calendar_event_get(Some(&chunk), None, Some(params.clone())).await?;
}
```

The calendars-client `Clone` derive supports this. The canonical mail-client does NOT — callers must rebuild the struct each iteration, or move-and-return via a helper, or wrap the params in their own Clone-able newtype. So the calendars-client direction is the better idiom.

## Why it matters

This is the canonical-template divergence direction that goes the *right* way — calendars-client made the better choice, and the divergence indicts the canonical, not the sibling. The workspace AGENTS.md propagation rule covers this: when a sibling diverges in a direction the canonical should adopt, the rule is "change the canonical first, then propagate".

Engineering basis:

1. Params structs are pure data — `Clone` is free, cheap, and zero-cost (the fields are `Option<bool>`-shaped, no allocations).

2. Real callers DO want to reuse params across multiple `/get` calls in a paginated or fan-out scenario. The current canonical pattern forces a rebuild per call.

3. Adding `Clone` to a public struct in a future canonical-template sweep is non-breaking. Removing it would be breaking. So the right time to settle the idiom is now, before the canonical ships at 0.1.x and the absence becomes the established contract.

## Filing as opinion-adjacent but not opinion

This is borderline taste — the canonical's omission of `Clone` is defensible (don't pay for what you don't use, smaller derive footprint). The calendars-client direction is also defensible (data structs should be `Clone` by default). The engineering argument is the canonical-template consistency: pick a workspace-wide policy. Currently calendars-client diverges silently with no documented rationale.

## Fix shape

Option A (preferred — calendars direction wins): add `Clone` to the five canonical mail-client params structs (`EmailGetParams`, `EmailCopyParams`, `MailboxSetParams`, `EmailSubmissionSetParams`, `EmailParseParams`). Note `EmailImportInput<'a>` already cannot derive `Clone` cleanly because of the borrowed-slice field — leave that one. Document the policy in mail-client's PLAN.md or AGENTS.md.

Option B: drop `Clone` from `CalendarEventGetParams` to match canonical. Lossier for callers but simpler propagation.

Either way, decide once at the workspace level so the canonical-template propagation rule is honoured.

## Source citations

- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/mod.rs:102 (Clone derive)
- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:40, 67, 87, 111, 253 (canonical without Clone)
title: `CalendarEventGetParams` derives `Clone`; canonical `EmailGetParams` does not — direction is right but the divergence is undocumented
